title: Project onto a line
prompt:
Write `project(B, a)`, which projects vectors onto the line through the vector `a`. Return `(P, R)`: the projections and the residuals `R = B - P`.

`B` is either one vector of shape (d,) or a matrix of shape (n, d) with one vector per row; `P` and `R` have the same shape as `B`. Raise `ValueError` if `a` is the zero vector. No Python loops.
hints: The projection of b is the multiple t·a that gets closest to b. What has to be true of the leftover piece, b − t·a, at the closest point?

At the closest point the residual is perpendicular to a: a · (b − t a) = 0, so t = (a · b) / (a · a). Dividing by ‖a‖ instead gives the length of the projection, not the multiplier. For many rows at once, `B @ a` computes every a · b in one product.
t = (B @ a) / (a @ a) has shape () or (n,). Then `P = np.asarray(t)[..., None] * a` scales one copy of a per row, and `R = B - P`.

misconceptions.projection-multiplier: The multiplier is (a · b) / (a · a). Dividing by ‖a‖ gives the scalar projection, the length of p, which equals the multiplier only when ‖a‖ = 1.
